# Testament of Asher — 10
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Asher's testament is the most philosophical of the twelve. He doesn't confess a major sin. He teaches a moral framework: the doctrine of the two faces.

**1** He was 125 years old, still healthy, when he gathered his sons.

**2** He said: I want to tell you what is upright before God. And it starts with this: God has built everything in twos.

**3** Two ways. Two inclinations. Two kinds of action. Two outcomes. Everything in this life has an opposite paired against it.

**4** Here's how the soul works: if a person orients toward the good inclination, all their actions come out righteous. Even when they sin, they repent quickly — their whole self is aimed at righteousness, so they shake off evil and pull out sin by the roots.

**5** But if a person orients toward the evil inclination, everything they do is corrupted — even their good deeds. They might start with something good and Beliar will twist the outcome into evil.

**6** This creates a paradox. There are actions that look evil but come from a good heart, and their end is blessing. There are actions that look good but come from an evil heart, and their end is destruction.

**7** Some examples of actions that look bad but are good:

A man refuses to show compassion to someone living in deliberate sin — that looks hard-hearted. But it's good, because enabling sin is not compassion.

A man hates someone who is "merciful" but also adulterous and practicing false fasting — he refuses to accept the partial goodness as truly good. That's good, because he follows the Lord's standard.

A man refuses to spend good days with people who revel, to keep his body and soul clean — that seems antisocial. But it's good.

**8** These people are like stags and deer — animals that look unclean by the rules but are actually clean, because they walk in zeal for God and stay away from what God forbids.

**9** But the reverse is also true: there are people who do "good" things from an evil orientation, and those good deeds get corrupted. Both spirits live in them, but the evil one dominates, and the good becomes poison.

**10** The double-faced people — they don't serve God. They serve their own desires, working to please Beliar and people like themselves. They pretend goodness but have no truth in them.

**11** So here is the takeaway:

Do righteous things. Store up treasure in heaven. Sow good things in your soul so you can harvest them in your life. Sow evil and you'll reap trouble.

**12** Get wisdom. Seek it in the fear of God. Because here's what survives catastrophe: not your property, not your city, not your gold — wisdom. If you keep yourself from evil, wisdom will be your honor among enemies, your home in a foreign land, your friend among foes.

**13** Whoever teaches this and lives it will be enthroned among kings — as Joseph was.

**14** After this he said: Bury me in Hebron. Then he fell into a deep sleep and died. His sons carried him to Hebron and buried him with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Asher*
